head: ac853df9
gate: Rejected experiment: routing a retained receive burst before draining handler commands
what_was_tried: After routing one event, the HTTP/3 concurrent owner looped up to 16 times over already-retained datagrams (Adapter.hasBuffered + Adapter.receive) before servicing the queued response commands, so ACK and stream progress for siblings would not wait behind up to 64 queued commands.

netz_only_harness.note: zio event loop, HandshakeServer.serveConcurrentStreams plus the client batch API, 1000 batches of 32

why_rejected: The same change hung the weft bench-h3 path after the sequential phase. A bounded 100us receive budget inside the drain still left the process sleeping with the client blocked in io_cqring_wait and the owner coroutine making no progress, so the burst drain interacts badly with response pacing and the single event loop. Shipping a 30% throughput win that can hang a server is not acceptable.
ruled_out: worker pool size: caps of 8 and 16 did not change 32-stream per-request throughput
server pacing ceiling: raising it to 1 GB/s changed batch32 from 146-153us to 137-143us
command wake latency: 0.4-12us after the wake race
event count per request: two at both batch widths
congestion-window growth: cwnd stays at the 10-packet initial value in both shapes because the sender is application-limited, which is RFC-correct
next_action: Coalesce response DATA across streams into fewer QUIC packets (or batch-route inside the cursor visitor while still draining commands between datagram groups) rather than draining datagrams ahead of the command queue.
